StackType.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 25.) The 15 `on_stack` no-op overrides are DELETED; the base `Power.on_stack` adds, matching PowerCmd.ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:236), which adds unconditionally with no StackType branch -- PowerStackType.Single means 'Amount is hidden and displayed as 1' (PowerStackType.cs:10-13), not 'does not stack'. All 16 units re-verified against their own C#: 15 are StackType.Single, and NONE overrides InstanceType (PowerModel.cs:144 default None), so none needs T1's instance machinery instead of amount-adding. Two per-site exceptions, both verified: (1) DAMPEN's C# StackType is actually `None`, not Single (DampenPower.cs:22) -- the queue's 16-unit list was wrong about it; its only applier, MagiKnight, dedupes caller-side (MagiKnight.cs:78-96: re-application calls AddCaster only and never reaches PowerCmd.Apply), so the deletion is inert through the real caller and T28's caster-set machinery is untouched and re-pinned. (2) HEX genuinely reads Amount (HexPower.cs:79 feeds CardCmd.Afflict<Hexed>(card, Amount)), so this deletion closes a real divergence that remains DORMANT only because SpectralKnight's move machine never loops back to HEX and KnightsElite fields exactly one -- a second Hex applier makes it live. ILLUSION needed no override and is unchanged (the opposite-sign case the record notes). No reachable re-application among the other 13: Burrowed and Soar re-apply only after their own expire/remove, always onto a fresh instance. Pins: test/test_stack_type_single.py (39 tests).  The text it replaced read: PowerStackType.Single, and the sim overrides Power.on_stack to `pass` citing it -- which is WRONG about C# and inert about this power. Single means only 'Amount is hidden, and is always 1' (PowerStackType.cs:10-13); PowerCmd.ModifyAmount:236 adds the offset with no StackType branch at all, so in the game a second application really does raise Amount to 2. This unit is one of the 15 the stack census flags (py audit/tools/power_census.py stack) and the main report's section 7 item 5 covers the class. DORMANT here for the per-unit reason the census leaves open: nothing reads this power's Amount -- not the power itself, not any sim listener, and not the C# model (whose only Amount reader is the hidden DisplayAmount). Named trigger: any future effect that scales with the stack count, or a UI that shows it. The one ported applier applies exactly 1 (cards/colorless_skills.py:770-772) and the power kills its owner the first time it fires, so a second stack is doubly unobservable.

AfterDamageReceived.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the death-prevention arm no longer floors HP. `_resolve_death`'s else-arm (cmds.py:51-64) leaves the creature dead at 0 HP -- CreatureCmd.cs:560-571 -- so cmds.py:185's `if not target.is_dead` now suppresses this hook on a prevented death exactly as CreatureCmd.cs:392 does; and where a preventer does heal, `CreatureCmd.kill` (cmds.py:284-292) re-enters `_resolve_death`, so the preventer gets the second say C# gives it. VERIFIED 2026-07-27 by reading cmds.py. WAS: the sim floored the owner at 1 HP and cleared is_dead, so this hook fired and killed the owner outright, bypassing the prevention the engine had just honoured.

guards.rationale: powers.py:3828 _expires before CreatureCmd.kill at :3829 -- the same order, and the order matters: removing first is what stops the kill's own damage path from re-entering this hook. The sim's _expire (powers.py:86-92) pops the power and unregisters it; C#'s PowerCmd.Remove (PowerCmd.cs:287-295) additionally fires power.AfterRemoved, which this power does not implement. Observationally identical, same treatment as the _expire entries in audit/records/power/duplication.json and audit/records/power/flame_barrier.json per binding rule 3.
cmds.py's CreatureCmd.kill. Same verb; the divergence in what the death pipeline then does is carried by the hook entry above rather than duplicated here.

powers.py:3826 is_powered_attack(props) (valueprops.py). Present and correct -- so unblocked POISON or Constrict damage does not trigger it on either side. Contrast power/thorns, whose port dropped exactly this gate.

The sim's on_damage_received amount is hp_lost, computed after block absorption and after modify_hp_lost (cmds.py:86-92), so `amount <= 0 -> return` (powers.py:3826) is the same test. A fully blocked attack does not kill the owner on either side.
